title: Context-aware paging and memory profile optimizer for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: For long-context workloads (8k-64k tokens) we see suboptimal GPU utilization and memory fragmentation across model variants (Llama 2/3 forks, Mistral, Qwen). Continuous batching interacts poorly with static KV residency heuristics: hot prefixes cause over-allocation, cold contexts pay for reserved KV slots, and quantized variants have different working-set sizes. Goal: implement a context-aware paging and memory-profile optimizer that adapts per-model and per-variant memory reservation, transparently pages nonhot KV segments to host memory or compressed stores, and provides a tunable policy exposed to the runtime and the Console for SLO/cost trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Automated per-variant memory profile generator added to runtime that produces a reservation plan for sequence lengths 2k/8k/32k/64k
Context-aware pager reduces peak GPU memory across evaluated Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants by >= 10% on average while keeping median token latency degradation <= 8%
Continuous batching throughput improves or matches baseline for mixed short/long workloads (no >5% regression across 99th percentile latency SLAs),
Instrumentation and Console dashboard updated to show paged slot counts, page-in latencies, and per-route cost delta
E2E tests added to CI with synthetic long-context traces and a smoke test for on-prem paging toggles
implementation_steps: 1) Model characterization: run automated profiler on selected model variants (llama-3-8k, mistral-7b-long, qwen-14k) to collect KV working set heatmaps
2) Design pager: implement async page-out of low-temperature KV slices to pinned host memory with optional compression (lz4) and background prefetch heuristics
3) Memory map: create per-variant memory reservation table with three bands (hot/resident, warm/prefetch, cold/paged) and an occupancy estimator
4) Integrate with batching: modify batch scheduler to mark request spans with expected prefetch windows so pager can preemptively page-in necessary slices
5) Telemetry & rollout: add tracing hooks, expose policy knobs in Console, and rollout via canary on dedicated pool
6) Benchmarks & tuning: run grid of batch sizes, quantized precisions, and context lengths to calibrate default profiles
benchmark_results: 2026-03-02: Profiling run on p4d-like instance (A100-equivalent), llama-3-8k: baseline peak GPU mem 38.6GB -> optimized peak 33.9GB (12.1% reduction); median token latency +4.6%; 95p latency +7.9%

2026-03-04: Mistral-7b-long quantized 4-bit: baseline peak 21.4GB -> optimized 18.6GB (13.1% reduction); throughput for mixed short/long batch improved by 6% due to freed capacity enabling larger concurrent batches
2026-03-06: Qwen-14k long-context: baseline peak 62.1GB -> optimized 56.8GB (8.5% reduction); observed page-in tail events that were fixed by increasing prefetch window from 32 tokens to 96 tokens
Summary: average peak memory reduction across variants: 11%; median latency impact: +5.1% across measured workloads; estimated per-token cost reduction: 9-14% depending on workload mix
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: aggressive paging reduces peak GPU usage but increases tail latency for cold context spikes; we mitigate by making prefetch window policy adaptive to request latency budgets
Compression (lz4) reduces host memory bandwidth but adds CPU overhead; for dedicated pools with limited CPU we expose compression as a knob
We avoid storing decoded KV on host to reduce complexity; pages are stored in compressed form and decompressed on page-in path to keep host footprint low
Fallback: if page-in latency exceeds threshold, route request to a warmer model variant or a Hosted pool with higher capacity (integrated with smart routing)
